title: Floats that print without a point in exponent form
notes: The YAML 1.2 Core schema reads `1E+17` as a float, but YAML 1.1 needs a point in the mantissa and a sign in the exponent, so PyYAML reads `1E+17` and `1e-5` as strings while it reads `1.0E+17` and `1.0e-05` as floats. A float is written with a point and a signed exponent whenever it is written in exponent form, so every reader reads a float. The Core-schema reading (loose) is the specification. The reading under YAML 1.1 and the number forms that some common readers accept (strict) is a writing convention of the family: a string is written plain only when it reads as that same string there too.

provenance.reference: The float 1e17 written as 1E+17, which PyYAML reads as a string; 1.0E+17 reads as a float.
